QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_55

question.text: Using the same Kalpataru data (Committed capital INR 50 cr, NAV Y3 INR 70 cr, hurdle 10% p.a., incentive fee 20%), BUT with a 100% CATCH-UP clause — amount distributed to the MANAGER:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ex 9.4 (100% catch-up): Total profit INR 20 cr; hurdle INR 16.55 cr; residual INR 3.45 cr. Manager's target total profit share = 20% × 20 = INR 4 cr. With 100% catch-up, ALL residual (3.45 cr) goes to manager until target (4 cr) is met. Since residual INR 3.45 cr < 4 cr, entire INR 3.45 cr goes to Manager. The Trap: Option A is the NO-catch-up outcome. Option C is the target share (unreachable here). Option B is total distribution. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B contrasts catch-up variants; XIX-C requires GP to negotiate. Manager's Pro-Tip: Insight from Ex 9.4: the SAME fund performance yields INR 0.69 cr (no catch-up) vs INR 3.45 cr (100% catch-up) to the GP — a 5× swing. This is why catch-up language is negotiated intensely.
